tracks.title: Jurisdiction and Removal
tracks.summary: Choose parties and forums, test personal and subject-matter jurisdiction, and decide whether removal or remand is available.
learningObjectives: Distinguish personal jurisdiction from subject-matter jurisdiction.
Apply complete diversity, amount in controversy, and the forum-defendant rule.
Explain when removal, remand, transfer, or dismissal changes the forum.
checkpoints: Before filing, identify the citizenship of every proposed party.
When removal is played, require the defense to name the original-jurisdiction basis.
During debrief, compare a forum-changing ruling with a case-ending ruling.

tracks.title: Rule 12 Motion Practice
tracks.summary: Sequence threshold defenses, identify waiver risk, and choose whether to oppose, cure, transfer, or amend.
learningObjectives: Match Rule 12 defenses to the facts that support them.
Recognize consolidation and waiver consequences for serial threshold motions.
Choose a procedurally responsive opposition or cure rather than a generic answer.
checkpoints: Ask the defense to state whether the objection is waivable before playing it.
Ask the plaintiff to identify whether the response defeats, cures, or redirects the attack.
During debrief, isolate every motion that answered the wrong defense.

tracks.title: Discovery and Rule 56
tracks.summary: Build an element-linked record with the right discovery tools, resolve objections, and test the record at summary judgment.
learningObjectives: Match depositions, production requests, admissions, and expert proof to specific proof needs.
Respond proportionally to burden, privacy, and privilege objections.
Explain why a missing proof item matters under Rule 56.
checkpoints: Require the plaintiff to name the proof item before selecting a discovery tool.
Pause after an objection and ask whether compulsion, narrowing, or a privilege log fits.
Close one round early so the class can observe a record-based Rule 56 loss.

tracks.title: Joinder and Supplemental Jurisdiction
tracks.summary: Test same-transaction party choices and whether related state claims can travel with a federal anchor claim.
learningObjectives: Connect same-transaction facts to permissive joinder choices.
Test whether a state claim shares a common nucleus with a federal anchor.
Recalculate diversity and removal consequences after a party is joined.
checkpoints: Ask what factual overlap supports the proposed party or claim.
Recalculate citizenship and the current court after joinder.
Compare the related wage claim with the unrelated rent dispute during debrief.

tracks.title: Erie and Class Actions Preview
tracks.summary: Introduce state-substantive versus federal-procedural choices and the threshold fit required for a class device.
learningObjectives: Identify the state-law right and the federal procedural mechanism in a diversity case.
State the basic Rule 23 fit questions without treating certification as automatic.
Separate preview-module issues from subject-matter jurisdiction and pleading questions.
checkpoints: Label each Erie choice as substantive or procedural before a card is resolved.
Require a Rule 23 reason before accepting a class-certification response.
During debrief, mark preview conclusions as provisional rather than a full doctrine treatment.
